tagline: Algiers, Oran and Béjaïa — a long Mediterranean port-city coast where the sea is the fastest line between the bays.
summary: Algeria fronts the Mediterranean along one of North Africa's longest coastlines, with life concentrated in its port cities: Algiers and its broad bay, Oran in the west, and Béjaïa and Mostaganem along the central and eastern coast. Coastal travel today runs on congested shore roads; a clean foiling tier adds a fast bay-and-coast layer between the city marinas and headlands on calm Mediterranean water, and Algeria is also the home of Yassir, the super-app that already moves daily mobility across these cities by phone.
why_marine_mobility: Algeria's population and economy ring a string of Mediterranean bays — Algiers, Oran, Béjaïa, Mostaganem — where the coast road is slow and the sea is direct. Navier's Pioneer II flies the urban-bay hops and short coast-to-headland runs, silent and zero-emission off the city ports, while the Quanta-LR range opens longer line-haul along the coast between the western, central and eastern port cities. It is an essential-mobility market with a fast-scaling digital ride-hailing habit and proven coastal demand.

demand_signals.label: Port-city bays
demand_signals.note: Algiers' bay, Oran's harbour, and the Béjaïa and Mostaganem waterfronts concentrate dense coastal demand where the shore road is the slow option.

demand_signals.label: Yassir's home market
demand_signals.note: Algeria is the birthplace of Yassir, the Maghreb super-app moving daily ride-hailing across these cities — the water leg is the natural premium extension of an existing digital habit.

demand_signals.label: Long coastline, slow road
demand_signals.note: One of the Mediterranean's longest national coastlines pairs scattered port cities with a congested coast road, leaving the sea as the directest line between bays.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling bay tier across the Bay of Algiers and the Oran harbour, linking the city waterfronts and headlands faster than the coast road.
A premium water leg booked inside Yassir alongside the car — extending the super-app onto the bay it cannot serve today.
Short coast-to-coast hops between the central and eastern port cities (Algiers–Béjaïa, Mostaganem–Oran) on fast, dry, zero-emission craft.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The urban-bay and short coast hops — Bay of Algiers runs, the Oran harbour, Béjaïa and Mostaganem waterfronts — sit inside Pioneer II's 70 nm all-electric range on calm Mediterranean water off the existing city ports.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The longer coastal line-haul between the western, central and eastern port cities extends into Quanta-LR's hybrid range, opening connections the all-electric craft cannot reach without charging dependency.

signature_routes.label: Bay of Algiers — port ↔ Sidi Fredj / Club des Pins (urban-bay run)
Oran ↔ Aïn El Turck (western harbour coast hop)
Béjaïa ↔ Cap Carbon / Aokas (eastern Kabylie coast run)

transit_planning: For Algeria's ports and merchant-marine administration, a city-port operator, or a coastal-tourism authority: a clean tier across the port-city bays and short coastal hops, off existing harbour infrastructure, complementing a congested shore road.
competitive_landscape: Coastal movement is by road and conventional port craft; there is no fast, clean, premium foiling tier across the city bays or between the port cities, leaving greenfield room on calm Mediterranean water with a digital ride-hailing base already in place.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under Algeria's transport ministry and port authorities. As a tag-only cluster today (boarding points and city pins, no sealed hero corridor yet), routes here are display-only until corridors are sealed — null beats confidently-wrong.
seasonality: A warm Mediterranean season (roughly April–October) drives peak coastal demand, with the bays calm and sheltered through much of the year; winter brings stronger seasonal winds that shape scheduling on the more exposed legs.
